newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-T&N shareholders to gain from deal.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-T&N shareholders to gain from deal.

text.p: The chairman of British-based automotive components group T&N Plc said on Wednesday that a huge insurance deal to cap its liabilities from asbestos health claims would remove constraints on future funds for dividends. "I really do think that at a stroke... we have produced the vision of an asbestos-free T&N," Sir Colin Hope told Reuters in a telephone interview

Commenting on the impact on the company's available funding for dividends he added, "It certainly does remove the constraints (on dividends) clearly, which we can take into account when we deal with the issue."
T&N plans to reduce the nominal value of its shares, in effect balancing out the impact of a one-off drop in group reserves caused by funding the insurance plan from provisions.
Hope said this was "essentially a technicality" but was being done in such a way that "the dividend position is absolutely secure and uninterrupted, meaning that dividends can continue".

As the plan covers all potential claims up to well over 1.0 billion stg, the company no longer expects to make any annual charges to its profit and loss account, in turn letting earnings per share and dividend cover rise substantially, Hope added.

The engineering company's health liabilities date back to its past as a miner and manufacturer of asbestos, used extensively in construction and automotive industries around the world earlier this century.

T&N, which has advanced as an efficient and profitable manufacturer of automotive components since Hope took the chair in 1989, has already paid out about 300 million stg for such claims over a period of years, all of them fully provided for. Hope said the acutarial assessment of future liabilities which underpins the new policy supported the firm's belief that the annual value of claims is likely to trend downwards.
"These actuarial assessments do tend to confirm what we'd said about the asbestos situation before -- that we're coming over the hump and beginning to go down," Hope told Reuters.
Asked if the 323 million stg of self-insurance T&N is to provide was so high that it may well not need to call on the insurance policy at all, Hope said this was quite likely.

"The actuarial asessment tends to say that we're not going to need it -- but what we were very conscious of was the fact that people were always saying "you don't know about what's going to pop up somewhere else'...For 92 million (the policy) removes all that uncertainty, and provide a very secure base."

"We've done it quite clearly to provided a separate fund that will act like a pension fund. If the performance (on asbestos claims)...is such that we don't require the money, the fund could build up a surplus," Hope said, adding it could also build up a surplus if its investment return was greater than expected.

However, he noted that the prospect of a surplus arising which could come back to the company "at some appropriate time" was against the background of an arrangement that is expected to run well into the next century. "The insurance is worldwide and without time limit. We're talking about (needing it until) 2020 or something," he added.
Looking at the way the fund would be created, Hope said it should certainly use no more cash that the ongoing asbestos liabilities would have done if T&N had kept on paying its way.
The arrangement should therefore provide the group with an steady base from which to seek "the same sort of satisfactory progress" from its components operations as in the past.

"Obviously we're not making any promises as far as future dividends are concerned, but emphasising that cover will improve and it's a matter of ensuring that the operating performance continues to improve, and the cash flow is adequate to do it."
